Of course there is little difficulty in distinguishing between the man in the upper photo and the rocks where he is attempting to hide. If he were our on the battlefield in France an enemy sniper wouldn't have much difficulty in spotting him off.

It would not be at all easy unless you had been told, to find that a man is hiding among the rocks in the lower photograph. Look close and you'll see that the small rock is not a rock at all but a man camouflaged to look like one. He's the same man as the one shown in the upper photo only this time his uniform is covered by the rock camouflage. It would be rather difficult for aAAAA to spot him now.

The man is a one member of the 1st and 2nd platoons of the camouflage class conducted by the New York Board of Education. He is showing the others just how camouflage works. Censored and passed by the Committee on Public Information.

PHOTO OF-A FLEET OF MODEL SHIPS FOR THE STUDY OF
CAMOUPLAGE.

NEWS ITEM-This photograph depicts the camouflage department of the U.S. Navy which was inaugurated at the beginning of the war in which all ships except battleships were camouflaged. The model room above contains models of every description, transports, submaring/chasers, colliers and merchant's ships all bearing some type of camouflage. The idea is to obtain a camouflage which would show up to the best advantage on the high seas. The models one at a time are placed into a room where a naval officer peering through a pellicope determines the effect on the painted sky, sea and clouds in the room. 4/3/19.

Providing of course that the German picks out the wrong target which he should for it is not possible to detect the difference between this "camouflage" soldier and the real trooper.

The designer and builder of this paper mache soldier is J.Burgess who is seen in the photo. He formerly was instructor of drawing in Syracuse University and now is a rookie officer, in training at Fort Sheridan, Ill. This paper mache soldier costs practically nothing but it could make the Teutons waste many bullet. Every bullet that dug its way in this dummy would surely be as good as a miss.
